D2C calculators tocheck your numbersbefore you spend.

Calculators and a plain-English glossary for D2C marketing. No email wall, no gated PDF: put your numbers in and take the answer with you.

Pick a toolOpen the glossary

In short

MMC's free tools are calculators and a glossary that help a D2C brand work out what a customer can cost, where the funnel leaks, and how long profit takes.

There is no email wall and no sign-up. Put your numbers in and take the answer with you.

  • Cost and profitUnit economics, break-even ROAS and LTV:CAC.
  • EfficiencyFunnel ROAS shows which step loses the most people.
  • Time and growthCAC runway and growth trajectory show how long and how far.
D2C calculators

Start from the decision, not the tool.

Each calculator is grouped by the question it helps you answer.

Can I afford to pay for a customer?

Cost and profit

Unit economics calculator

What you may be doing instead

Looking at revenue per order and not at what is left after COGS, fulfilment, RTO and CAC.

Use this when

You want to know whether one order really contributes, and the volume you need to break even.

Open the calculator

Break-even ROAS calculator

What you may be doing instead

Chasing a ROAS number you heard somewhere, instead of the one your own cost sheet gives.

Use this when

You are setting or judging a ROAS target and want the exact break-even, and the one that hits your target margin.

Open the calculator

LTV:CAC calculator

What you may be doing instead

Judging a customer by the first order alone.

Use this when

You plan to keep customers and want to see the month your acquisition cost is paid back.

Open the calculator

Efficiency

Funnel ROAS calculator

What you may be doing instead

Use this when

Use this when

You are launching or relaunching and need to know how long it takes to turn, and how much cash it burns.

You want to see where today's run rate actually gets you.

Open the glossary

Screens on this page are illustrative recreations, not real results.

Reading the results

A number is not a verdict.

Nothing here judges your brand. It shows the shape of the problem and the order worth fixing it in.

Use your own numbers

Start from your cost sheet and your ad account, not from a figure you heard elsewhere. Your break-even is specific to you.

Change one input at a time

Move one number, see what changes, then move the next. That shows which lever matters most.

Count returns and fees

RTO, shipping and gateway fees quietly reduce what an order leaves behind. Put them in before you trust a result.

Which order to run them in

Start with unit economics: if one order does not contribute, nothing downstream matters. Funnel ROAS then shows where efficiency is lost, break-even ROAS shows the efficiency you need, and LTV:CAC shows how patient you can afford to be. CAC runway answers how long a new brand burns before it turns, and growth trajectory projects the margin forward.

Common questions

What people ask about the tools.

Are the tools free?

Yes. There is no email wall and no gated download. You put your numbers in and see the answer.

Which calculator should I start with?

Start with unit economics. If one order does not contribute, nothing downstream matters. Then use break-even ROAS for the efficiency you need and LTV:CAC for how patient you can be.

Is the result a verdict on my brand?

No. A number shows the shape of the problem and the order worth fixing it in. It does not judge your brand.

Can MMC run these numbers with me?

Yes. Book a strategy call and bring the question that is stuck.
